title: Comparison inverse image commutes with scheme pullback
statement:
For $u:U\to V$ there is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \nu_U^*u_{\Et}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 u_{\Proet}^{-1}\nu_V^*.
$$

It is compatible with identity maps, composites, and the cartesian
identification in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

proof.text:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be the chosen square of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and put $F\in\Sh(Y_{\Et})$. The required compatibility says that the two paths from $
u_{X'}^*f'_{\Et}{}^{-1}g_{\Et}^{-1}F$ to $g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}f_{\Proet}^{-1}
u_Y^*F$ agree: first use $c_{f'}$, then $f'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}c_g$, then $	heta_{\square}^{\Proet}$; or first use $
u_{X'}^*	heta_{\square}^{\Et}$, then $c_{g'}$, then $g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}c_f$. To spell out the specified square identification, write $k_{a,b}:(ba)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}a^{-1}b^{-1}$ for the composition identification constructed in step 3. Then $	heta_\square=k_{g',f}\circ k_{f',g}^{-1}$, with the middle inverse-image functors identified by $fg'=gf'$. This is the cartesian identification of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; on the pro-etale site use the same formula with its composition identifications. Thus each occurrence of $	heta$ in the two paths reduces to the composition comparisons already checked in step 3. Apply the Hom bijections of step 2 and the composite adjunction to both paths. On an etale object $W/Y$, their right-image maps compare the sections over $(W	imes_YY')	imes_{Y'}X'$ and $(W	imes_YX)	imes_XX'$. Both schemes identify with $W	imes_YX'$ by the maps with projections to $W$ and $X'$. The map between them is uniquely characterized by preserving these projections; the condition $fg'=gf'$ supplied by $\alpha$ gives exactly that map for both paths, whether the inclusion into the pro-etale site is made before or after the base changes. Thus their section maps, their restriction maps in $W$, and therefore their maps on $\operatorname{Hom}(F,-)$ are equal. Injectivity of the adjunction bijections proves equality of the two left-image paths. This retains the specified $\alpha$ and proves the cartesian compatibility, in each of the coefficient categories already treated.
